Rule 11 keeps the ASV italics from making 'be' added; rule 17 heads on the adjective.

Second member of the coordinated subject; the article at s002 governs the whole phrase and 'Father' stands on its own word (rule 26).

Rule 20 displacement: tou kyriou hemon -> 'of our Lord'. The genitive pronoun hemon is free, carrying only the possessive, so rule 76's availability test is met and 'our' belongs to it; the article realizes nothing and 'of' stays with the noun.

ton oiktirmon -> 'of mercies': the ASV supplies the noun no determiner, so the article has no English 'the' to anchor and is unrepresented under rule 23. Rule 21 forbids leaving a bare 'of' on it, so the case preposition stays with the noun, exactly as tes eirenes -> 'of peace'.
Source noun rendered 'of + noun'; the supplied 'of' realizes the genitive case and rule 17 heads on the noun.
Expressed conjunction aligned in the ordinary way.
Anarthrous noun with no supplied determiner; stands on its own English word.
Attributive quantifier standing on its own English word (rule 26). Rule 58 is not in question: 'all' is the adjective's own rendering, not a supplied determiner for the phrase.
Anarthrous noun: the supplied 'of' realizes the genitive case and rides with the noun under rule 21, discontinuously across the intervening quantifier under rule 15. Rule 17 heads on the noun.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: every unit in the accepted alignment survives the check, and no edge, status or head was altered.

Partition verified: s001-s018 and t001-t020 each appear exactly once, no invented IDs, every aligned unit has nonempty source and target with both heads inside their arrays, and both unrepresented units are source-only with a valid source head and a null target head.

The two unrepresented articles rest on different rules and both were re-tested. s006 is rule 20 displacement, and rule 76's availability test confirms it: hemon carries only 'our' and has not been spent on any other role, so the possessive has a source word to belong to. s013 is rule 23, the ASV writing no determiner at all before 'mercies'; rule 21 explicitly forbids leaving a bare 'of' on such an article, so the case preposition stays on the noun in both cases. A reference comparison may report either article as a disagreement; neither is a correction.

s001's copula placement was checked against rule 63 rather than rule 53 alone, since the subject is a lexical noun phrase rather than a pronoun. Rule 53's noun-phrase exception is scoped to a subject pronoun, so 'be' stays with the predicate adjective and is not read off the ASV's word order.

The marginal reading 'Or, God and the Father' would move the s002 article's construal onto pater, but rule 12 bars a new textual decision inside the alignment file; the projection was aligned as supplied and the note recorded here only.
